question: Prompt 3: does a protein-level second pass for unnamed eDNA reads have a buyer?
rule_fixed_before: Worth a conversation if one provider's unassigned-read pass reaches USD 50,000 a year at a price they already charge for an add-on; method paper otherwise. Step 3 kill: every study under 10% unnamed at genus.
result_under_rule: Worth a conversation when price is multiplied by one provider's sample count (step 5 method); read strictly, not yet met: no add-on price exists and uptake is not shown. Step 3 does not kill: five marine studies, 14.8% to 87% unnamed at genus.
evidence: Wilderlab comprehensive minus basic panel = USD 68 per sample (a tier step, not an add-on); 736 samples a year reach USD 50,000; Wilderlab runs about 8,700 (running-total average) to 20,000+ samples a year, all panels include COI. Second-agent check: 7 failures in draft, all fixed.
caveat: Protein k-mers reach only COI amplicons and shotgun reads, not 12S/16S/18S or qPCR. Whether translated COI names genera was not tested (Prompt 2).
